intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Santorini Caldera Beach Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a day exploring the unique volcanic beaches of Santorini, including the famous Red Beach and Black Beach (Perissa). Swim in crystal-clear Aegean waters surrounded by dramatic volcanic cliffs. Rent a sunbed and umbrella and soak in the stunning caldera views that make Santorini world-famous.

experiences.name: Athens Street Food Tour in Monastiraki
experiences.description: Dive into Athens' vibrant street food scene in the bustling Monastiraki neighborhood. Sample souvlaki wraps, spanakopita, loukoumades (honey-drenched doughnuts), and fresh gyros from legendary local vendors. Wash it all down with a cold Greek frappe while browsing the lively flea market stalls.

experiences.name: Navagio Shipwreck Beach Visit
experiences.description: Take a short boat excursion to the iconic Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach, one of the most photographed beaches in the world. Enclosed by towering white limestone cliffs and accessible only by sea, this secluded cove features impossibly turquoise water and a rusted shipwreck resting on pristine white sand.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class & Market Visit
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local Cretan family. Start with a guided tour of the vibrant Chania Municipal Market to select fresh ingredients — olives, herbs, local cheeses, and seafood. Then learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos, lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled loukoumades.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Pink Sand Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Journey to the breathtaking Elafonissi lagoon on the southwestern tip of Crete, famous for its shallow turquoise waters and unique pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and shells. Wade across the shallow lagoon to the small island, snorkel among colorful marine life, and relax on one of Greece's most stunning and naturally preserved beaches.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at destination airport, collect luggage, and take a budget-friendly public bus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea right outside the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the nearby harbor or village waterfront. Explore the local area on foot, find the nearest taverna strip, and enjoy a relaxed first evening soaking in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap gyros wrap or tiropita (cheese pie) from a kiosk or bakery near the airport or bus station (€2–4)
meals.dinner: Find a local taverna near the resort and try a classic Greek salad, grilled sardines, and house wine — look for daily specials on a chalkboard menu (€10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Rest and acclimatize. Exchange some euros at the airport if needed — avoid hotel exchange desks. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy the resort's included breakfast if available, or head to a local bakery for a spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee (€2–3). Head to the nearest public beach early to claim a good spot — avoid paying for sunbeds by bringing your own towel and finding a free sandy stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling in the crystal-clear Aegean waters. Walk along the coastline to explore quieter coves. If there is a local beach bar, enjoy a fresh lemonade or frappe (€2–3).
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest village center for an evening passeggiata (evening stroll). Browse local shops and find a family-run taverna for dinner away from the tourist strip.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery — spanakopita and Greek coffee (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a supermarket — olives, feta, bread, tomatoes, and bottled water (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Family-run taverna: moussaka or pastitsio with a side of tzatziki and pita bread, local draft beer (€11–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reusable water bottle and refill it — Greece has good tap water in most areas. Supermarket picnics are a great budget hack for lunches throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a cheap bicycle to explore a nearby village inland. Visit the local morning market (laiki agora) if one is running — a fantastic way to see local life, taste free samples, and buy cheap fresh fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a historic church or small archaeological site in or near the village — most are free or cost under €3. Wander through narrow whitewashed alleyways and take photos of bougainvillea-draped doorways.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Sit at a seafront café and watch the sunset with a glass of ouzo or local wine. Dine at a mezedhes (small plates) restaurant and share several dishes.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the market plus a koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor (€2–3)
meals.dinner: Meze dinner: dolmades, taramasalata, grilled octopus, and saganaki (fried cheese) shared between two — pair with local retsina wine (€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus schedules the night before. Buses in Greece can be infrequent — plan your return time carefully to avoid getting stranded.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — head to a different beach from Day 2, ideally one reachable by a short walk or bus. Look for a less-touristy, quieter beach for a more local experience. Swim and relax in the 29°C sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a paddleboard or kayak from a local water sports shack (€8–12/hour) for some light adventure on the water. Alternatively, join a free or low-cost group snorkeling session if available locally.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from the local supermarket if your accommodation has kitchen facilities — grilled vegetables, feta, and crusty bread. Otherwise, grab souvlaki from a street grill.

meals.breakfast: Homemade or resort breakfast — boiled eggs, bread, olives, and coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar: toasted sandwich (tost) and fresh orange juice (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki street grill: two pork skewers with pita and chips (€6–8 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Souvlaki and gyros stalls are the best budget meal option in Greece — filling, delicious, and usually €2–4 per piece. Identify your nearest one early in the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local ferry or public bus to a nearby island or coastal town (research the closest ferry port to your resort). Arrive and explore on foot — most Greek island towns are compact and walkable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at a recommended beach on the day-trip island or town. Have lunch by the water. Explore the Venetian or Ottoman old town if one exists — history is free to walk through.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the return ferry or bus before sunset. Arrive back at the resort and enjoy a quiet dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — Greek coffee and a tiropita from a bakery (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a harbor-side taverna on the day trip — ask for the catch of the day, which is usually the cheapest option (€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Simple and light back at base — supermarket mezedes: hummus, pita, olives, and cold cuts (€5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry or bus timetables in advance and book return tickets early in the day. Day trips by ferry are often very affordable in Greece (€10–20 return).

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and have a slow morning at the resort. Enjoy the beachfront location — swim before the crowds arrive. Read a book under a beach umbrella or explore the hotel's immediate surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to a local fishing village. Watch the fishermen bring in their catch, browse any small craft stalls, and visit a tiny whitewashed chapel if you find one.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor event, local music performance, or cultural gathering if one is happening in the nearest town — check local notice boards or ask hotel staff. Otherwise, enjoy a relaxed taverna dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort or bakery breakfast — freddo cappuccino and a bougatsa (custard pastry) (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Fishing village snack — fresh bread, local cheese, and a cold beer from a mini-market (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner: grilled sea bream (tsipoura) with lemon potatoes and a village salad (€13–17 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ask your hotel staff for insider tips on free local events — Greeks are very hospitable and happy to share recommendations. Many villages hold free festivals and outdoor cinema nights in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local archaeological site, ancient ruins, or a Byzantine castle within reach of your resort. Entry fees are often free for EU citizens under 25 and low-cost for others (€3–8). Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for swimming. The sea is warm and perfect in late June. Find a shaded café near the beach for a mid-afternoon frappe and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to mark the halfway point of the trip — find a well-reviewed local restaurant and try something you haven't eaten yet, such as lamb kleftiko or fresh lobster pasta.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey and fresh figs from a café (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Packed supermarket lunch at the ruins: crackers, olives, feta, cucumber, and water (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge dinner: lamb kleftiko or fresh pasta with local seafood, a carafe of house wine (€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Halfway through the trip — a great time to review your spending and adjust if needed. Greece's archaeological sites are often stunning even without a guide; download a free audio guide app before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning swim before breakfast — the sea is glassy and calm in the morning. Then visit a local open-air market or artisan street if one runs on this day of the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or e-bike (€15–25/day) and explore the coastline independently, stopping at hidden beaches and viewpoints that are inaccessible by bus. This is one of the best ways to see Greece on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Find a clifftop or hillside spot to watch the sunset — one of Greece's most iconic experiences and completely free. Then head to a harbor taverna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bakery run: cheese pie, olive bread, and a Greek coffee (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Roadside grill or village kafeneion (traditional coffee house): grilled pork chops and village fries (€7–10)
meals.dinner: Harbor taverna: shrimp saganaki (prawns in tomato and feta sauce) with crusty bread and local white wine (€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental requires a valid license in Greece. Always wear a helmet — it is legally required and fines are common. Check fuel levels before heading out to remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day — head to the most scenic beach you have discovered so far and spend the morning swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing. Practice floating in the salty Aegean — the high salinity makes it effortless.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a walk along a coastal hiking trail if one is accessible from your beach. Many Greek islands and coastal areas have well-marked footpaths with stunning sea views. Bring plenty of water.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner at the resort or accommodation if kitchen facilities are available — try making a simple Greek salad and pan-fried feta with honey. Otherwise, visit a gyros shop for a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket supplies: fresh bread, honey, sliced tomatoes, and instant coffee at the resort (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Beach snack: watermelon slice from a vendor, a cold can of Mythos beer, and a bag of chips (€4–6)
meals.dinner: DIY Greek dinner at accommodation or gyros shop: two large gyros wraps with chips and a cold drink (€8–10 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated in the 29°C heat — drink at least 2 liters of water per day. Avoid hiking in the midday sun (12:00–15:00). Apply SPF 50 sunscreen and reapply after swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the nearest large town or city for a change of scenery. Explore the central square (plateia), the local church or cathedral, and any free museums. Walk through the old neighborhood and admire the neoclassical architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse a local street food market or covered food hall. Try regional specialties you haven't encountered yet. Pick up some edible souvenirs — local honey, dried herbs, or olive oil — which are far cheaper than tourist shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in the town before returning to the resort. Eat where locals eat — look for restaurants with Greek-only menus on a chalkboard, no pictures on the menu, and filled with local families.

meals.breakfast: Town bakery: loukoumades (honey doughnuts) and a Greek coffee (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Street food market: try a variety of small bites — grilled corn, fried calamari, and a sesame koulouri (€5–8 total)
meals.dinner: Local family taverna in town: daily special (mageirefta — oven-cooked dishes like gemista or fasolada bean soup), bread, and a beer (€9–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mageirefta (oven-cooked dishes) are the cheapest and most authentic meals in Greek tavernas — they are made fresh each morning and often sell out by afternoon. Ask what is available as soon as you sit down.

day_by_day.morning: Return to a favorite beach for one last long morning swim. The sea is warm and the weather is perfect. Take time to snorkel, collect shells, or simply float and enjoy the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove, vineyard, or small farm if one offers tours or tastings near your resort. Many offer free or very cheap visits (€5–10) with tastings of olive oil, wine, or local produce included.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a seafront taverna — choose a spot with a view of the water and order a full Greek spread to celebrate the second-to-last full day in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and a freddo espresso at a beachside café (€4–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the farm or olive grove tasting, or pack supermarket supplies (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Seafront taverna feast: mixed grilled seafood platter, Greek salad, tzatziki, bread, and a bottle of local white wine shared (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to buy any remaining souvenirs. Avoid airport and tourist-area shops — local supermarkets and village shops sell the same Greek products (honey, olive oil, herbs) at a fraction of the price.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — wake up early and head straight to the sea for a sunrise swim. This is one of the most magical experiences Greece offers and it is entirely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon packing, doing any last-minute souvenir shopping, and revisiting your favorite local spot — a café, a viewpoint, or a quiet alley that made an impression during the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Greece — return to the best taverna you found during the trip and order your favorite dishes. Raise a glass of ouzo or local wine to a successful budget adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final bakery visit: fresh tiropita, a koulouri, and a Greek coffee (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Light supermarket lunch or leftover supplies to clear out the room (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite taverna of the trip — order freely within budget and enjoy the last Greek meal (€14–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure flight details tonight. Confirm transfer arrangements to the airport for the next morning. Set an alarm and keep your passport and boarding pass accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final quick breakfast before heading to the airport. Take one last look at the Aegean Sea before departing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to the airport. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your departure flight. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Greek treats (honey, olive oil, or mastiha products) which can be good value at Greek airports.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 days of beaches, local food, and authentic Greek experiences — all on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast: a cheese pie and coffee from a bakery near the hotel or at the airport (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring supermarket snacks to the airport (€5–8)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep all receipts for any VAT refund claims if applicable. Greece offers VAT refunds to non-EU travelers on purchases over €50 from participating stores — ask for a Global Blue form at the time of purchase.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs and collect luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea right outside the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the nearby harbour or waterfront promenade to soak in the sunset. Explore the closest village square (plateia) and enjoy your first evening in Greece at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a casual seaside snack bar near the resort upon arrival — try a classic Greek spanakopita or tiropita (cheese pie) from a local bakery.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range taverna near the resort. Order a mezze spread: tzatziki, taramasalata, grilled octopus, and fresh bread. Pair with a carafe of local house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Prioritise hydration and a good night's sleep. Exchange currency or withdraw euros at the airport ATM if needed.

day_by_day.morning: After a resort breakfast, spend the morning at the resort's beachfront. Swim in the warm Aegean, snorkel along the shoreline, or simply relax on a sun lounger. Water temperature is ideal for extended swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local town or village on foot or by local bus. Visit the central market (agora) to browse fresh produce, olives, honey, and local spices. Pop into a small deli to taste regional cheeses.
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset boat trip or a short harbour cruise if available locally — a great way to see the coastline from the water as the light turns golden.

meals.breakfast: Buffet or included breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Greek yogurt with thyme honey and fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local taverna in the village: grilled fish of the day (psari) with horta (wild greens) and lemon potatoes.
meals.dinner: Seaside restaurant dinner — try lamb chops (paidakia) or moussaka with a Greek salad. Budget around €20–30 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen — the June sun at 29°C is intense, especially on the water. Bring a hat and sunglasses for afternoon walks.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk or light jog along the beach before the heat builds. Visit a nearby archaeological site or historic church/monastery within the area for cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon — rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local water sports rental near the resort. Explore hidden coves along the coastline accessible by water.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town for an authentic Greek evening. Walk the old quarter, admire traditional whitewashed architecture, and browse small artisan shops for local ceramics or olive wood souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — try loukoumades (Greek honey doughnuts) if offered, or pick up fresh koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar lunch — fresh gyros wrap with pork or chicken, tzatziki, tomato, and onion. Very affordable at €4–6 each.
meals.dinner: Traditional psarotaverna (fish taverna) dinner — grilled sea bream (tsipoura) or sea bass (lavraki) served whole with olive oil and lemon. Pair with chilled Assyrtiko white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Water sports rentals are typically €15–25/hour. Book early in the morning to secure equipment during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day guided or self-guided tour to a significant local historical or cultural landmark in the region (ruins, ancient theatre, or hilltop fortress depending on location). Bring water and wear comfortable walking shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a mid-afternoon swim and rest during the hottest part of the day (2–4 PM). Read, nap, or enjoy a cold frappe at the resort bar.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking experience or food-focused evening: look for a local cooking class or food tour where you learn to make traditional dishes like dolmades, dakos, or fresh tzatziki.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — load up before the morning excursion.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a village kafeneion (traditional café) stop during the cultural tour — order a village salad and a cold Mythos beer.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the cooking class venue or a highly rated local taverna nearby. Enjoy what you made, or order slow-cooked lamb kleftiko and roasted vegetables.

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically cost €50–80 per person and are bookable online or through the hotel concierge. Highly recommended for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — find a quieter, less touristy beach nearby (ask hotel staff for local tips). Bring a picnic bag with snacks from the local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a scenic coastal walking trail or nature path in the area. The warm weather and low rainfall make June perfect for light hiking. Look for wildflowers, olive groves, and sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local winery or olive oil producer for a tasting session if available in the region. Many Greek islands and coastal areas have boutique producers offering informal tastings.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a village bakery — fresh tiropita, koulouri, and a Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes).
meals.lunch: Picnic on the quiet beach — pick up olives, feta, crusty bread, cherry tomatoes, and cold cuts from the local market.
meals.dinner: Relaxed taverna dinner back near the resort — try pastitsio (Greek baked pasta with meat sauce) or stuffed peppers (gemista) for a hearty homestyle meal.

day_by_day.notes: Ask hotel staff about hidden beaches — locals always know spots that don't appear on tourist maps. Bring reef shoes if the beach is pebbly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip preparation: take an early ferry or local boat to a nearby island or coastal village for a full day of exploration. Depart by 9 AM to maximise time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip destination — wander narrow alleys, visit a local church or windmills, swim at a recommended beach, and browse small shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to base. Arrive at resort by early evening, shower, and enjoy a quieter dinner close to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departure — grab a yogurt and fruit to go.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the day-trip destination — fresh seafood at a harbour-front restaurant. Try grilled calamari, shrimp saganaki (in tomato and feta sauce), and a Greek salad.
meals.dinner: Low-key dinner at a resort-area taverna — souvlaki platter with pita, fries, and tzatziki. Simple, satisfying, and affordable.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets for short hops typically cost €10–25 each way. Check the return schedule carefully to avoid missing the last boat back.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, enjoy a slow resort breakfast, and spend time at the pool or beach with a good book. Midweek rest is important on a 13-day trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local open-air market if one runs on this day (check with hotel). Stock up on local honey, herbs, saffron, and handmade goods as potential souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar or rooftop venue if available nearby. This is Greece — sunsets are a serious event. Enjoy a glass of ouzo or a local aperitif.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — take your time and enjoy the spread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a nearby café — a mezze plate with hummus, olives, and warm pita, plus a cold lemonade.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for a mid-range restaurant dinner — try a seafood risotto, grilled whole fish, or a creative modern Greek menu. Budget €35–45 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a good day to reflect on the first half of the trip and plan any remaining activities, book tours, or make dinner reservations for the second week.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkelling session — either off the beach or on a guided snorkel tour. June water clarity is excellent. Look for sea urchins, small fish, and underwater rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cultural afternoon: visit a local folklore museum, Byzantine church, or traditional craft workshop to learn about regional history and artisan traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event if available — outdoor cinema, live Greek music (rebetiko or laïká), or a village festival. Check local listings or ask hotel staff.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up before the snorkelling session.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a casual waterfront café — try a dakos salad (Cretan rusk with tomato, feta, and olives) and a cold Fix beer.
meals.dinner: Traditional meze dinner at a local taverna — order 5–6 small dishes to share: saganaki (fried cheese), gigantes (giant beans), grilled vegetables, and meatballs (keftedes).

day_by_day.notes: Snorkel gear can often be rented from beach kiosks for €5–10/day. Guided snorkel tours run €25–40 per person and include equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Hire a scooter, ATV, or rent a car for the day to explore the wider coastal area independently. Drive along scenic coastal roads, stop at viewpoints, and discover beaches not accessible on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a secluded cove or beach discovered during the morning drive. Spend a few hours swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the privacy of a less-visited spot.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back and freshen up. Head out for dinner in a neighbouring village or town you spotted during the day's exploration.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast from a local bakery before picking up the vehicle — fresh pastries and a strong Greek coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic at the secluded beach — buy supplies at a village mini-market: bread, cheese, olives, fruit, and cold water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the village taverna you scouted earlier — try whatever the daily special is (ask the owner). Freshness and simplicity are the hallmarks of great Greek cooking.

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs €20–35/day; ATV €40–60/day; small car €45–70/day. Always check insurance coverage and wear a helmet. Fuel up before heading to remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — swim, relax, or take a gentle yoga session on the beach if the resort offers it. Enjoy the simple pleasure of the warm Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Food-focused afternoon: visit a local olive oil mill, honey producer, or cheese maker for a behind-the-scenes look at traditional Greek food production. Many offer tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner at one of your favourite tavernas from the trip so far — revisit a place you loved and order dishes you want to savour one more time.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy the full spread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the food producer visit — tastings and samples often serve as a satisfying informal lunch.
meals.dinner: Return to your favourite taverna — order a full feast: starter mezze, main course, dessert (loukoumades or galaktoboureko), and finish with a complimentary shot of raki or ouzo from the owner.

day_by_day.notes: Many small producers are family-run and appreciate genuine interest in their craft. Learning a few words of Greek (efharisto = thank you, yamas = cheers) goes a long way.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning — this is your dedicated 'do absolutely nothing' day. Swim, read, listen to music, and enjoy the sun. No schedules, no tours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon spa treatment at the resort or a local wellness centre — a traditional Greek massage or a salt scrub using local sea salt and olive oil is a perfect mid-trip treat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach followed by dinner at a casual beachside restaurant with your feet practically in the sand.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — slow and leisurely.
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch — fresh salads, a cold sandwich, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Keep it light.
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner — grilled octopus, a fresh Greek salad, and chilled white wine as the sun sets over the water. Pure Greece.

day_by_day.notes: Resort spa treatments typically cost €50–90. Book in advance as they fill up quickly in peak season. This day is intentionally unstructured — embrace the Greek concept of 'siga siga' (slowly, slowly).

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: take a boat trip to a nearby sea cave, lagoon, or marine park for swimming and snorkelling in crystal-clear waters. Many local operators run half or full-day trips.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from boat trip. Use the afternoon for last-minute souvenir shopping — look for high-quality local products: extra virgin olive oil, thyme honey, mastiha products, or handmade jewellery.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory final dinner at the best restaurant you've identified during the trip. Dress up slightly, order the full experience, and toast to a wonderful Greek holiday.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the boat departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the boat — most full-day boat trips include a BBQ lunch on board or a stop at a seaside taverna. Fresh-grilled fish and salad.
meals.dinner: Best restaurant of the trip — splurge on a memorable final meal. Try a tasting menu or chef's selection if available. Order a bottle of Assyrtiko or Xinomavro wine. Budget €45–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips cost €40–80 per person depending on duration and inclusions. Book 2–3 days in advance. For souvenirs, avoid airport shops — local market prices are far better and more authentic.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last swim in the Aegean. Pack bags, check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, and store luggage with the concierge if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a local café, take a last walk along the beach, or simply sit and absorb the atmosphere one final time.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport. Depart Greece with wonderful memories, a suitcase of local treats, and a deep appreciation for Greek beaches, food, and hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or a local bakery stop — one last Greek coffee and tiropita.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or airport — a gyros wrap or a simple salad to keep things easy on travel day.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane — save room in your bag for any Greek snacks (olives, nuts, dried figs) to enjoy on the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Use any remaining euros on local food products at the airport duty-free or keep them for a future trip. Yamas — cheers to Greece!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at destination airport, meet private transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort, and enjoy a scenic chauffeured ride to the hotel. Check in, receive a welcome amenity (chilled towel, champagne, fresh fruit), and settle into your beachfront suite. Take a leisurely first stroll along the private beach to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Unwind with a sunset cocktail at the resort's clifftop bar, watching the golden Aegean light fade over the water. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at the resort's signature restaurant to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light mezze platter and fresh-squeezed juice at the resort's beachfront lounge upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant – grilled whole sea bass with lemon-herb oil, local horta greens, and chilled Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: Request early luggage drop if suite is not yet ready. Ask concierge to pre-book all restaurant reservations and experiences for the coming days.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to a lavish breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the sea. Afterward, enjoy a guided snorkeling excursion departing from the resort's private jetty – explore crystal-clear coves, sea caves, and vibrant marine life with a professional guide and top-tier equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a light lunch, then spend the afternoon on the private beach with a premium sun lounger and cabana service. Order chilled drinks and fresh fruit platters delivered to your lounger. Optional: take a paddleboarding lesson with the resort's water sports instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest charming harbor village for an authentic evening. Browse boutique shops and watch local fishermen return with the day's catch before sitting down for dinner at a celebrated harborside taverna.

meals.breakfast: Extensive à la carte breakfast on your private suite terrace – Greek yogurt with Cretan thyme honey, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light mezze at the beach bar – tzatziki, grilled halloumi skewers, Kalamata olives, and village bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated harborside taverna – fresh catch-of-the-day grilled over charcoal, stuffed vine leaves, tomato-feta salad, and a carafe of local Moschofilero rosé

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling excursion the night before through the concierge. Sunscreen SPF 50+ strongly recommended – UV index will be very high.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided food market tour in the nearest town. Visit the covered fresh market with a local chef guide, sampling seasonal produce, local cheeses (graviera, manouri), cured meats, olives, and regional honey. Purchase artisan products to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a private Greek cooking class hosted by the chef guide at a traditional stone farmhouse. Learn to prepare spanakopita, slow-braised lamb kleftiko, and a classic semolina halva dessert using the morning's market ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner on your suite terrace or the resort's secluded garden, served by your personal butler.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant – freshly baked tiropita, local jams, cold cuts, seasonal fruit, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared during the cooking class, accompanied by chilled local beer or wine
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or garden dinner curated by the resort chef – lobster linguine with ouzo-cream sauce, grilled asparagus, and a premium Greek dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: Confirm cooking class numbers in advance; classes are typically limited to 8 guests for an intimate experience. Wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes for the market.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private yacht charter departing from the resort's jetty. Sail to secluded sea caves and hidden beaches inaccessible by land. The yacht includes a captain, deckhand, and onboard chef. Morning swim stop at a pristine turquoise cove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht journey to a second hidden beach for snorkeling and sunbathing. Enjoy a freshly prepared onboard lunch with seafood caught that morning. Sail back along the coastline as the afternoon light turns golden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort refreshed. Treat yourself to a 90-minute couples' or solo Aegean Sea spa ritual at the resort spa, incorporating volcanic stone massage and local olive oil treatments.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure – Greek yogurt parfait, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Onboard the yacht – freshly grilled octopus, shrimp saganaki, village salad, chilled white wine, and fresh watermelon
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's seafood terrace restaurant – whole roasted Mediterranean sea bream, saffron-infused orzo, and a bottle of premium Domaine Sigalas Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up. The concierge can arrange the yacht charter with 24 hours' notice. Confirm dietary preferences with the onboard chef in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Guided hike along a scenic coastal trail with a local naturalist guide. The trail offers panoramic views of the Aegean Sea, wildflowers, and ancient terraced olive groves. Moderate difficulty; approximately 2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional family-run olive oil estate nearby. Enjoy a private tour of the ancient olive trees and stone press, followed by a premium olive oil tasting paired with local breads, cheeses, and cured fish.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort pool as the sun sets. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at the pool bar before heading to an acclaimed nearby restaurant known for its modern Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the hike – energy-boosting granola, hard-boiled eggs, seasonal fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Olive oil estate tasting lunch – artisan breads, aged graviera, smoked sardines, fresh tomatoes drizzled with estate extra-virgin olive oil, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Modern Greek tasting menu at a celebrated local restaurant – 6-course menu featuring deconstructed moussaka, Aegean prawn carpaccio, slow-cooked lamb with wild herbs, and baklava soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking sandals or trainers for the coastal hike. Bring a reusable water bottle – the concierge can prepare a chilled flask. Purchase olive oil at the estate to take home as a premium souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy breakfast in bed, then spend the morning floating in the sea or lounging in the private cabana. Optional: sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's wellness instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to a nearby ancient archaeological site or hilltop Byzantine monastery. A specialist art-history guide provides an in-depth, exclusive tour avoiding the main tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening at the resort's cellar bar. The sommelier presents a curated flight of six premium Greek wines – from Nemea's Agiorgitiko reds to Crete's Vidiano whites – paired with artisan charcuterie and local cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in bed – freshly baked spanakopita, smoked salmon bagel, Greek yogurt with honey, and a pot of mountain tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional kafeneion (coffee house) near the archaeological site – hearty bean soup (fasolada), grilled lamb chops, and village salad
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort's wine bar – premium charcuterie and cheese boards, warm pita, fig jam, and walnut bread alongside the wine tasting

day_by_day.notes: Request the resort's private archaeology guide at least 2 days in advance. The wine tasting can accommodate specific preferences – inform the sommelier of any dislikes beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private speedboat to a nearby uninhabited island or remote beach. Spend the morning completely alone on pristine white sand with a packed luxury picnic basket prepared by the resort chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel the surrounding reefs, swim in the clear shallow lagoon, and simply relax in total seclusion. The speedboat returns mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the resort, enjoy a long sunset dinner at the resort's most exclusive dining venue – a cliffside table for two with unobstructed sea views, reserved exclusively for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure – croissants, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Luxury picnic on the uninhabited island – chilled lobster, artisan cheeses, prosciutto, marinated vegetables, fresh fruit, and a bottle of chilled rosé Champagne
meals.dinner: Cliffside fine-dining dinner – amuse-bouche, seared scallops with saffron foam, slow-roasted lamb rack with truffle jus, Greek cheese course, and a decadent dark-chocolate and mastic ice cream dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is the trip's most romantic and memorable day – ideal for a special occasion. Ask the resort to arrange a flower arrangement or personalized message at the cliffside table if celebrating.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure. Indulge in a 2-hour spa morning: begin with a hammam steam ritual, followed by a full-body exfoliation using Aegean sea salt and olive oil scrub, ending with a relaxing aromatherapy massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local ceramics studio or artisan workshop in a nearby village. Enjoy a private hands-on pottery class learning traditional Greek techniques, and take home your own handmade piece as a keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an authentic Greek music evening at a local taverna or cultural venue – live bouzouki and traditional folk music with dancing. Join in or simply enjoy the vibrant atmosphere with locals.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet – eggs made to order, smoked fish, fresh pastries, cold cuts, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at a village square café – lamb souvlaki wraps, grilled vegetables, tzatziki, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Dinner at the live music taverna – mezze feast of dolmades, fried zucchini chips, grilled calamari, slow-cooked goat stew, and house barrel wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the ceramics class through the concierge. The pottery piece can typically be shipped home if too fragile to carry. Arrive at the music taverna by 21:00 for the best atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided sea kayaking tour along the coastline, exploring sea arches, grottos, and hidden coves. Suitable for all fitness levels; guided by a certified marine guide with safety equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for lunch and a long, indulgent afternoon at the beach. Treat yourself to a premium beach service package – chilled towels, afternoon cocktail service, and a beachside fruit platter.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a rooftop restaurant in the nearest town for dinner, offering sweeping panoramic views of the coastline and Aegean horizon as the stars emerge.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before kayaking – Greek yogurt, banana, granola bar, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort – fresh grilled octopus, crispy calamari, village salad, and chilled Mythos beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Rooftop dinner – tuna tartare with capers and lemon oil, charcoal-grilled swordfish steak, roasted potato wedges with garlic and rosemary, and a glass of premium Santorini Nykteri white wine

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking departs early morning to avoid midday heat. Waterproof phone case recommended. The rooftop restaurant requires a reservation – book through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided day trip to a nearby historic town or island (by private speedboat or chauffeured vehicle). Explore a UNESCO-listed old town, ancient ruins, or a traditional whitewashed village with a specialist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse local artisan boutiques and specialty food shops in the historic town. Purchase premium local products: saffron, aged cheeses, artisan honey, hand-woven textiles, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a final sundowner at the clifftop bar before a memorable dinner at a renowned local chef's restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure – full Greek spread with tiropita, cold cuts, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at a celebrated restaurant in the historic town – braised rabbit stifado with pearl onions, roasted root vegetables, and a carafe of local red wine
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at a renowned local restaurant – intimate 7-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring hyper-local seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the historic town exploration. Carry a light linen layer as some churches or monasteries may require covered shoulders.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Final long swim in the warm Aegean Sea, followed by a beachside yoga and meditation session. Spend time journaling, reading, or simply absorbing the beauty of the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sunset sailing cruise on a traditional Greek caïque (wooden sailing boat). Sail along the coast, stop for a final swim in a secluded bay, and enjoy chilled drinks on deck as the sun descends.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a celebratory farewell dinner at the resort's finest table, reflecting on the journey with exceptional food, wine, and ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast in bed or on the terrace – eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and a pot of Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the caïque – chilled shrimp cocktail, artisan bread, local cheeses, and chilled Champagne
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at the resort – premium seafood tower, grilled whole lobster with herb butter, truffle risotto, and a decadent dessert platter with mastic panna cotta and baklava

day_by_day.notes: Request a special farewell setup from the resort (flowers, personalized menu card, or a complimentary bottle of wine) to mark the end of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim and breakfast at the resort. Pack and prepare for checkout. Visit the resort spa for a final express treatment – a 45-minute refreshing facial or foot massage before the journey home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout if available (confirm with resort). Spend remaining time at the pool or beach. Private chauffeured transfer to the airport departs in the early-to-mid afternoon depending on flight schedule.
day_by_day.evening: Airport lounge access arranged by the resort concierge. Depart Greece with unforgettable memories.

meals.breakfast: Final grand breakfast at the resort – full spread including made-to-order eggs, pastries, smoked fish, and a farewell glass of fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport lounge – mezze platter, fresh salad, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: In-flight or at airport lounge depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout at least 48 hours in advance. Confirm private transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Allow extra time at the airport during peak summer season.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day / travel buffer day. If the return flight is delayed or you have opted for an extra night, use this day for any last-minute shopping for premium Greek souvenirs: extra-virgin olive oil, Mastiha products, saffron from Kozani, or fine Greek wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: if still in Greece, enjoy one final long lunch at a waterfront taverna before heading to the airport. Alternatively, this day serves as a comfortable travel recovery day upon returning home.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home rested and inspired, with memories of pristine beaches, extraordinary food, warm Aegean waters, and world-class luxury hospitality.

meals.breakfast: If still in Greece – final Greek coffee and a koulouri (sesame bread ring) at a local bakery or café
meals.lunch: If still in Greece – farewell waterfront lunch: grilled sea bream, horta, village salad, and a final glass of Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: In-flight or at home

day_by_day.notes: This buffer day is intentionally light to allow for travel flexibility, rest, and any last-minute experiences. It also accommodates any flight delays or changes to the return schedule.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC
